title.value: New Results on the φ-Hiding Assumption and Factoring Related RSA Moduli
New Results on the φ-Hiding Assumption and Factoring Related RSA Moduli

abstract.value: In this paper, we first propose a rigorous polynomial time algorithm based on the univariate Coppersmith theorem that factorizes an integer N = P Q r with unknown primes P, Q and r ≥ 1, for an arbitrary given prime e > N 1 4r satisfying e | φ(N). Furthermore, the bound e > N 1 4r is improved to e > N β-rβ 2 if the value of β such that Q ≥ N β is known. Moreover, these two bounds can also be obtained respectively when e is no longer a prime number. Specifically, we address the scenario where e is a square-free composite number with known factorization, as well as the case where e is a composite number with known factorization, and the corresponding prime factors P and Q of N satisfy gcd(P-1, Q-1) = 2. In both cases, in order to make the corresponding algorithms polynomial time, we limit the number of prime factors of e to O(log log N) and r to be any integer constant. When applied to the φ-hiding assumption, our bounds are significantly better than previous results. When applied to standard RSA moduli, we extend the case where e, which was involved in the previous best bound e > N 1 4 , is no longer a prime number. This can highlight the security vulnerability introduced by the function RSAN,e, as discussed by Kakvi et al. in [23], being at least ei-to-1 lossy for some prime factors ei of e. When applied to decompose the semi-smooth RSA subgroup moduli, we provide a rigorous proof for the second bound presented by Naccache and Stern for the first time. We validate the effectiveness of algorithms through experiments.

In this paper, we first propose a rigorous polynomial time algorithm based on the univariate Coppersmith theorem that factorizes an integer N = P Q r with unknown primes P, Q and r ≥ 1, for an arbitrary given prime e > N 1 4r satisfying e | φ(N). Furthermore, the bound e > N 1 4r is improved to e > N β-rβ 2 if the value of β such that Q ≥ N β is known. Moreover, these two bounds can also be obtained respectively when e is no longer a prime number. Specifically, we address the scenario where e is a square-free composite number with known factorization, as well as the case where e is a composite number with known factorization, and the corresponding prime factors P and Q of N satisfy gcd(P-1, Q-1) = 2. In both cases, in order to make the corresponding algorithms polynomial time, we limit the number of prime factors of e to O(log log N) and r to be any integer constant. When applied to the φ-hiding assumption, our bounds are significantly better than previous results. When applied to standard RSA moduli, we extend the case where e, which was involved in the previous best bound e > N 1 4 , is no longer a prime number. This can highlight the security vulnerability introduced by the function RSAN,e, as discussed by Kakvi et al. in [23], being at least ei-to-1 lossy for some prime factors ei of e. When applied to decompose the semi-smooth RSA subgroup moduli, we provide a rigorous proof for the second bound presented by Naccache and Stern for the first time. We validate the effectiveness of algorithms through experiments.
